title: Touching Jupiter
caption: Reaching for Jupiter at Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A person stands on the telescope platform at Paranal and stretches a hand toward what looks like a bright star in a sky crowded with stars. The figure is ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek, and the bright point is not a star at all but the planet Jupiter.

The playful pose hides a big difference in distance. Jupiter is tens of thousands of times closer to us than the stars around it in the picture. Seen from Earth, a planet and a star can look much alike, both as points of light, even though one lies within our Solar System and the others are far beyond it.

ESO's Paranal Observatory sits on top of Cerro Paranal in Chile, which puts it, as ESO says, really close to the stars. The background, full of stars, shows off the exceptionally clear, dark skies of northern Chile.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: Jupiter is easy to see with the naked eye, but a long exposure brings out many more faint stars around it than a person would see.

explore: One way to tell a planet from a star by eye is that planets usually shine with a steadier light, while stars tend to twinkle more as their light passes through the atmosphere.
alt: A person on an observatory platform reaching toward a bright point of light, the planet Jupiter, in a star-filled sky.
